assumptions: Documents: the first n_docs fit-half documents in doc_id order that reach max_tokens tokens under the model's tokenizer (the C1 length filter); shorter ones are skipped and listed. Report-half lines are never parsed.
States: c3.traces.masks.uniform_masks with min_masked = max(k) = 8, so every state can commit 8 positions; realised rates are recorded.

Ranking on real text by the exact log-odds ell (as c3.traces.masks.topk_confidence; ties to the lower position). On the probe by the grid's own rule (float32 top-1 probability, ties to the lower field) so that the states and commit sets are the grid's.

The sequential chain fills earlier ranks with the model's own sequential (greedy) tokens, not the true tokens. Every argmax is over the full vocabulary with [MASK] excluded (SUBS), on the probe too (not restricted to a field's values).

Per document: the mean over its committed positions. On real text every state contributes exactly k, so this is also the mean over its states. On the probe a trajectory commits each field once, so it is disagreements / fields, the counterpart of the grid's A_per_field.
(B) proxies are also reported at k = 1 (the most confident position); disagreement at k = 1 is reported only as a check (0 by construction).

Probe calibration: confidence-rule cells only (the proxy's set is the k most confident positions); the k = 1 cells are left out of the Spearman (both quantities 0 by construction). Point Spearman against the grid JSON's A_per_field; its interval resamples instances within each rho, one resample shared by every k and both quantities, with (A) per instance recomputed on the same states. |(A)| < 1e-12 nats is treated as 0 (exactly 0 analytically at rho = 0; the float residue would otherwise be ranked).
No torch deterministic settings, as scripts/run_probe.py, so the probe passes are the grid's; probe batches and length groups are the grid's (--probe-batch-size 32).

At rate 1.0 every document's input is the all-[MASK] sequence, so the parallel and sequential tokens (hence the disagreement) are identical for every document there; only Delta and CE vary. per_k therefore weights one shared state 1/10; per_k_rates_below_1 gives the same estimands over rates 0.1-0.9 (same resamples).
